name: Beef Bourguignon Pasanda
description: Beef bourguignon pasanda combines French slow-braise technique with Pakistani whole spices and a papaya-yogurt marinade. Halal, alcohol-free, and deeply flavoured.
keywords: beef bourguignon pasanda, beef pasanda recipe, french pakistani beef stew, bourguignon pasanda, halal beef stew, no alcohol beef braise, papaya marinated beef
recipeIngredient: 1 kg (2.2 lb) beef shin or chuck, cut into 5 cm pieces
80 g (3 oz) raw green papaya, grated
50 ml neutral oil or clarified butter
Small handful flat-leaf parsley, roughly chopped

recipeInstructions.name: Marinate the beef
recipeInstructions.text: Combine grated papaya pulp, yogurt, salt, white pepper, cumin, and coriander in a large bowl. Add the beef pieces and coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for 4 to 6 hours.

recipeInstructions.name: Bring beef to room temperature
recipeInstructions.text: Remove the beef from the refrigerator 45 minutes before cooking.

recipeInstructions.name: Brown the shallots
recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add shallots cut-side down and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden. Remove and set aside.

recipeInstructions.name: Bloom the whole spices
recipeInstructions.text: In the same pot over medium-low heat, add cardamom, black cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf, peppercorns, and star anise. Stir for 60 to 90 seconds.

recipeInstructions.name: Cook garlic and ginger
recipeInstructions.text: Add sliced garlic and minced ginger to the spices. Stir for 2 minutes until pale gold.

recipeInstructions.name: Brown the beef in batches
recipeInstructions.text: Scrape excess marinade off the beef. Brown in two batches over medium-high heat, about 3 minutes per side until deep mahogany. Transfer to a plate.

recipeInstructions.name: Build the tomato base
recipeInstructions.text: Add chopped tomatoes and tomato paste to the pot. Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until thick, dark red, and beginning to separate from the oil.

recipeInstructions.name: Add chilli powder
recipeInstructions.text: Stir in the kashmiri red chilli powder and cook for 1 minute.

recipeInstructions.name: Deglaze with verjus
recipeInstructions.text: Pour in the verjus and scrape the bottom of the pot to lift the fond. Reduce for 3 minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Return beef and add stock
recipeInstructions.text: Return the browned beef to the pot. Pour in the beef stock until liquid reaches two-thirds up the meat. Bring to a gentle simmer.

recipeInstructions.name: Add shallots and braise
recipeInstructions.text: Return the browned shallots to the pot. Cover tightly and cook on lowest possible simmer for 2 hours, checking every 45 minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Check for tenderness
recipeInstructions.text: After 2 hours, test the beef with a fork. It should yield without resistance. If not, cook for a further 30 to 45 minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Reduce and finish the sauce
recipeInstructions.text: Remove beef and shallots. Increase heat and reduce the braising liquid for 10 to 12 minutes until it coats a spoon. Adjust salt. Off heat, stir in butter and lemon juice.

recipeInstructions.name: Serve
recipeInstructions.text: Return beef and shallots to the pot and warm through for 2 minutes. Scatter with flat-leaf parsley and serve over basmati rice, naan, or egg noodles.
